body:
I refactored the course editor to use react forms and zod validation since @nicolarevelant made a strong point by pointing out the complexity of the previous course editor which was already quite unmaintainable.

Thanks to zod, the whole validation schema is defined on a type which depends on the DTO for course creation. This validation is defined through a nice and readable syntax in the file `src/components/course/CourseEditor/schema.ts`.

Then, the central component `CourseEditModal` combines the various sections contained in the `EditCourseSections` folder and wraps them around a **FormProvider**. This allows all the subcomponents to attach to the provided form via appropriate hooks. All these functionalities are provided by the react-hook-form library. 

Make sure to run `pnpm install` to add the new libraries.

# Overview

**Type of Change:** New Feature & Bug Fix

**Summary:** This pull request enhances the Artwork Gallery panel with several UI improvements and functional updates. Key changes include adding sorting options (Alphabetical, Last Updated), a manual refresh button, refining text and spacing for better readability, and ensuring thumbnails consistently regenerate upon refresh. Additionally, the main canvas rendering now dynamically adjusts its vertical position based on the height of the active panel below it for improved visual centering. A bug where thumbnails disappeared on refresh has also been fixed.

## UI/UX Implementation

The following UI/UX changes were made to the `GalleryPanel`:

1.  **Text Updates:**
    *   The placeholder text "Saved artwork will appear here." was replaced with "Note: Custom Colors may be inaccurate in thumbnails below."
    *   The "Note:" text font size was reduced (using `.caption`).
    *   The "Note:" text is now centered.
2.  **Layout Adjustments:**
    *   The vertical spacing between the "Artwork Gallery" title and the "Note:" text was reduced.
    *   A sorting segmented control (Alphabetical/Last Updated) was added below the "Note:", centered horizontally.
    *   A refresh button (↻ icon) was added, positioned to the right of the sorting control and aligned with the right edge of the artwork thumbnails below.
    *   Spacing was adjusted to add a small gap below the "Note:" text and reduce the gap between the sorting/refresh controls and the artwork grid.
3.  **Dynamic Canvas Centering:**
    *   The main `CanvasView` now shifts its content slightly higher when the taller `GalleryPanel` is open compared to when other, shorter panels are open. This provides better visual centering relative to the available space above the panel.

## Model Updates

### Data Models

No changes were made to the underlying data models.

### Object-Oriented Models

*   **`GalleryPanel.swift`:**
    *   Added `@State` variable `sortOption` of type `SortOption` (new enum) to manage the selected sorting state.
    *   Added `SortOption` enum (`alphabetical`, `lastUpdated`).
    *   Added `sortedArtworkItems()` computed property to return artwork items sorted based on `sortOption`.
    *   Modified `loadArtwork()` to clear the `thumbnails` dictionary and explicitly call `generateThumbnails()` upon successful fetch to ensure re-rendering.
    *   Modified the action closure for the main gallery header button to call `loadArtwork()`.
    *   Modified the `drawShapes()` helper function (for thumbnails) to calculate `centerY` as `size.height * 0.45` to shift the rendering slightly upwards within the thumbnail bounds.
*   **`CanvasView.swift`:**
    *   Modified the `canvasVerticalOffset` computed property. It now returns different negative offset values depending on whether `showGalleryPanel` is true or if one of the other panels (`showProperties`, `showColorShapes`, `showShapesPanel`) is true, allowing the canvas offset to adapt to panel height.

*(No updated diagrams provided)*

## End-to-End Testing Instructions

1.  **Build and Run:** Launch the application on a simulator or device.
2.  **Open Gallery:** Tap the gallery icon (photo stack) in the bottom button bar.
3.  **Verify Initial UI:**
    *   Confirm the title is "Artwork Gallery".
    *   Confirm the note text reads "Note: Custom Colors may be inaccurate in thumbnails below.", is centered, and has a smaller font size.
    *   Confirm the sorting control (Alphabetical | Last Updated) is present, centered below the note. "Last Updated" should be selected by default.
    *   Confirm the refresh icon (↻) is present to the right, aligned vertically with the sorting control and horizontally near the right edge of the thumbnails.
    *   Observe the spacing between the title, note, sorting controls, and the artwork grid.
4.  **Test Sorting:**
    *   If you have multiple saved artworks with different titles and save times, tap "Alphabetical" and verify the artwork reorders alphabetically by title.
    *   Tap "Last Updated" and verify the artwork reorders by save time (most recent first).
5.  **Test Refresh Button (↻):**
    *   Tap the refresh button (↻).
    *   Verify that the thumbnails briefly disappear and then reappear (indicating regeneration). The loading indicator might flash briefly. The sorting order should remain applied.
6.  **Test Gallery Header Button Refresh:**
    *   While the gallery panel is open, tap the main gallery icon (photo stack) in the *header* section of the panel (not the bottom bar).
    *   Verify that the thumbnails refresh similarly to step 5.
7.  **Test Thumbnail Rendering Center:**
    *   Observe the artwork within the thumbnails. Confirm the visual center appears slightly higher than the geometric center of the thumbnail square.
8.  **Test Dynamic Canvas Centering:**
    *   Observe the main artwork visible *behind* the gallery panel. Note its vertical position.
    *   Tap the "X" button to close the gallery panel.
    *   Tap one of the other panel buttons (e.g., sliders for Properties, stack for Color, squares for Shapes).
    *   Observe the main artwork visible behind the newly opened (shorter) panel. Confirm that its vertical position is slightly *lower* than it was when the gallery panel was open.
    *   Tap the "X" button again. Verify the artwork returns to its fully centered position when no panel is open.
9.  **Save/Load (Implicit):** Although not directly changed, ensure saving new artwork and loading existing artwork still functions correctly via the gallery interactions (tapping a thumbnail to load).

## Description

Adds the `--save` and `--save-as` flags to allow users to save their current CLI flag configuration to a `ffg.config.jsonc` file.

-   `--save`: Saves the current flags (excluding transient/control flags) as the `defaultCommand` in `ffg.config.jsonc` in the current working directory.
-   `--save-as <name>`: Saves the current flags under the specified `<name>` in the `commands` section of `ffg.config.jsonc`.

This enables easy reuse of complex configurations.

-   Updated CLI argument parsing in `src/cli.ts` to handle the new flags and ensure they trigger config saving *before* analysis runs.
-   Added logic in `src/index.ts` (main function) to prepare flags, update the config object (loading existing if present), and write it back using `src/utils.ts`. Only explicitly provided or merged flags (excluding control flags like `--save`, `--save-as`, `--pipe`, etc.) are saved.
-   Modified `src/utils.ts` to include `writeFfgConfig` and ensure `loadFfgConfig` handles JSONC.
-   Added new tests in `test/config-save.test.ts` to cover various saving scenarios (new file, overwrite default, overwrite named, merging with `--use`).
-   Updated `README.md` with documentation for the new flags and configuration file features.
-   Fixed a minor regex issue in `test/whitespace-flag.test.ts` discovered during testing.

## Problem

The current `generate_simple_dataset_docs.py` script has several issues:
1. It uses SimpleCopickDataset which is no longer preferred
2. It's very slow due to loading the entire dataset and caching
3. It processes more samples than needed just to generate examples

## Solution

This PR replaces the slow script with a much faster implementation that:

1. **Uses only MinimalCopickDataset**: Removes dependency on SimpleCopickDataset
2. **Limits sample scanning**: Stops processing once it finds examples of each class
3. **Improves efficiency**: Processes only a small fraction of the dataset
4. **Adds timing information**: Reports execution time for performance tracking
5. **Focuses on essentials**: Collects just one example per class for faster processing

## Performance Improvement

The new implementation is significantly faster because it:
- Doesn't load and cache the entire dataset
- Stops scanning after finding enough examples
- Uses a small max_samples value (50) to limit processing
- Avoids processing unnecessary data

## Implementation Details

The changes include:
1. A new `generate_dataset_examples.py` script that replaces `generate_simple_dataset_docs.py`
2. Updated README references to point to the new script and documentation structure
3. A new test file `test_dataset_examples.py` aligned with the new implementation

- All pickable objects have examples

body:
Addresses #4878

We have encountered an issue with duplicate users when it comes to granting tribal access. We realized that duplicate users are inevitable, and here's why.

Login.gov does not allow multiple accounts to share one email address. However sometimes, a user will delete their account on Login.gov and start a new account. When this user logs into the FAC with a new account (but the same email), we have no way of guaranteeing what the situation is, other than that Login.gov is giving us a unique username... therefore we create a new (but duplicated) user. Logically, the most recently active user (going off of `last_login`) is the most up-to-date account.

This PR makes some fixes in Django admin to recognize this case and continue to operate without failure.
- When generating staffusers, ALL users tied to the emails passed in `staffusers.json` are considered. Only the most recently active user is created into a `StaffUser`.
- When generating a `UserPermission` based on an email, if the email is tied to more than one user, the `UserPermission` is assigned to the most recently logged in user.

This PR also exposes Django admins to the `User` table with read-only access. This is so we can quickly identify duplicate users in our system without the need to perform an SSH operation.

## How to test

1. Log into the local app to generate your user. Then, manually insert (or modify existing user emails) to create duplicate emails of your Login.gov email.
2. Make sure your email is in `staffusers.json`. Then, upon running the `create_staffusers` management command, ALL of the users with your email should have `is_staffuser = true`.
3. Confirm you exist as a `StaffUser` in Django admin.
4. Now that you have multiple users with the same email, try creating/editing/deleting a `UserPermission` with your email. You should encounter a successful response rather than an error.
5. Visit the Users table on Django admin and make sure it is a read-only table. Try sorting/searching, and clicking into users to make sure the correct content is displayed.

- [ ]   List any special steps reviewers have to follow to test the PR. For example, adding a local environment variable, creating a local test file, etc.
- [ ]   For extra credit, submit a screen recording like [this one](https://github.com/GSA-TTS/FAC/pull/1821).
- [ ]   Make sure you’ve merged `main` into your branch shortly before creating the PR. (You should also be merging `main` into your branch regularly during development.)
- [ ]   Make sure you’ve accounted for any migrations. When you’re about to create the PR, bring up the application locally and then run `git status | grep migrations`. If there are any results, you probably need to add them to the branch for the PR. Your PR should have only **one** new migration file for each of the component apps, except in rare circumstances; you may need to delete some and re-run `python manage.py makemigrations` to reduce the number to one. (Also, unless in exceptional circumstances, your PR should not delete any migration files.)
- [ ]   Make sure that whatever feature you’re adding has tests that cover the feature. This includes test coverage to make sure that the previous workflow still works, if applicable.
- [ ]   Make sure the full-submission.cy.js [Cypress test](https://github.com/GSA-TTS/FAC/blob/main/docs/testing.md#end-to-end-testing) passes, if applicable.
- [ ]   Do manual testing locally. Our tests are not good enough yet to allow us to skip this step. If that’s not applicable for some reason, check this box.
- [ ]   Verify that no Git surgery was necessary, or, if it was necessary at any point, repeat the testing after it’s finished.
- [ ]   Once a PR is merged, keep an eye on it until it’s deployed to dev, and do enough testing on dev to verify that it deployed successfully, the feature works as expected, and the happy path for the broad feature area (such as submission) still works.
- [ ]   Ensure that prior to merging, the working branch is up to date with main and the terraform plan is what you expect.

## PR Checklist: Reviewer

- [ ]   Pull the branch to your local environment and run `make docker-clean; make docker-first-run && docker compose up`; then run `docker compose exec web /bin/bash -c "python manage.py test"`
- [ ]   Manually test out the changes locally, or check this box to verify that it wasn’t applicable in this case.

- [ ]   Verify that no Git surgery is necessary at any point (such as during a merge party), or, if it was, repeat the testing after it’s finished.

The larger the PR, the stricter we should be about these points.
